dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you?
Hi, Kevin. Good afternoon. How is your day going so far? Is it a busy one for you?
It's been steady, Friday before the holidays and the phones haven't stopped. Thanks for asking. What's going on?

Okay, so I am calling about the water in the street. The rain that finished yesterday, Thursday, the big one, and now the water it is still here. At the end of my block there is a low spot, and it is under maybe a foot of water. A foot, I am not exaggerating.
A foot, okay. Let me get that down. What street are you on?
Mill Street, in the Historic Hill. I am at 161 Mill Street. The low spot is at the end of the block, where the street goes down.
161 Mill Street, end of the block, low spot, about a foot of standing water. And is that from the storm drain not taking it, do you think?

Yes, I think the drain is not taking it. Every time it rains hard, the same thing. The cars they have to go very slow, and the water goes up to the sidewalk. Nobody comes to fix. I want that somebody come and look.
Understood. Has it been like this a while, or just since this storm?
Not just this storm. It happens again and again, with the heavy rain. This time is bad because yesterday it rained so much. But the water, it does not go down even now. It is Friday already.
Yeah, that's a long time for it to sit. Okay, I'm writing: drain at the low point not draining, water still there a day after the storm. Anything else you can see from where you are?

Yes, one more thing. There is a manhole cover, near the water, and it looks off. Not sitting right. Maybe one inch, it is higher or moved, I don't know how to say. When the car goes over, it makes a noise.
Okay, so the manhole cover looks off by about an inch and it clunks when cars go over it. Is it in the water, or beside it?
Beside it, a little bit before the water. I did not go close, because the water is there. But I see it from the sidewalk. So it is not covered by water, you understand? It is before.
Got it, just before the flooded part. That one I'll flag separately so they look at the cover as well as the drain. Somebody could hit that or it could shift more.
Yes, exactly, this is what I am worried they do not see. So you will send somebody today? Or I must wait for the next week?
I'll get it in to the crew supervisor as soon as we hang up. They're prioritizing after the storm, so there's a list. I'd expect somebody to take a look today or early next week.
Early next week. Okay. Let me ask you, the crews, they work on the weekends? Because if it is Saturday and Sunday and the water is still there, it is no good.

They do cover emergencies on weekends. If the water's rising or the cover becomes dangerous, call us or the main line and say it's a safety issue, and that gets handled differently than a routine request.
Okay, so if it is more danger, I call again on Saturday. I understand this right?
That's right. Tell them it's a hazard with the manhole and reference today's report.
Okay. I am a little frustrated, I tell you honestly. I call before, and I see nothing change. The drain, it is the same.

I hear you. I don't see an earlier ticket on my screen for this address from you, but I'm putting plenty of detail in this one so the crew knows it's a repeat spot. I'll note the end of the block, the drain, and the cover.
Good. Please write that it is every time with big rain. Every time.
Writing that. Recurs with heavy rain. Now, do you want a callback once it's assigned? I'd need a number.
401-555-0158. And the name?
Teresa Cabral. Cabral, C-A-B-R-A-L.

Teresa Cabral, got it. So I have 161 Mill Street, low spot at the end of the block under about a foot of water, drain not clearing, plus a manhole cover off by an inch just before it. Did I get that right?
Yes, that is right. Thank you. One thing, if the water goes in the cars, it is the city problem, no? I am only asking, to understand.
I can't speak to claims on this line, but if anything gets damaged, write down the date and take photos. Someone in the right office can tell you the process.
Okay, photos. I will do. Thank you, Kevin. Have a good weekend.
You too, Teresa. Stay out of that water. Bye now.
